accepted.s: Which department manages the Central Government's equity in Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) and conducts disinvestment through methods such as strategic sale and Offer for Sale?
o: Department of Investment and Public Asset Management
accepted.x: The Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM), under the Ministry of Finance, manages the Centre's equity in CPSEs and conducts disinvestment.
accepted.tq: Identify the department associated with the specific function.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment - DIPAM, strategic sale vs minority stake sale, New PSE Policy 2021

accepted.s: DIPAM was renamed from the Department of Disinvestment in which year?
accepted.x: The Department of Disinvestment was renamed as DIPAM in 2016.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the establishment year from the later renaming year.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment - DIPAM, strategic sale vs minority stake sale, New PSE Policy 2021

accepted.s: The National Investment Fund was set up on:
accepted.x: The National Investment Fund was established on 3 November 2005.
accepted.tq: Use the precise date rather than the date of a later disinvestment event.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment - DIPAM, strategic sale vs minority stake sale, New PSE Policy 2021

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding forms of disinvestment:
1. In minority disinvestment, the Government retains more than 51 per cent ownership and management control.
2. In majority disinvestment, management control is transferred while the Government retains a minority stake.
3. Strategic sale involves transfer of a block of shares along with management control to a strategic partner.
4. Complete privatisation involves sale of 100 per cent ownership and control.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly distinguish minority disinvestment, majority disinvestment, strategic sale and complete privatisation.
accepted.tq: Classify each form by ownership retained and management control transferred.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment - DIPAM, strategic sale vs minority stake sale, New PSE Policy 2021

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: IPO — further issue by an already listed PSE
OFS — auction of shares on the stock exchange
IPP — issue open to all retail investors
accepted.x: Offer for Sale (OFS) is an auction of shares on the stock exchange. IPO is a first-time public issue, FPO is a further issue by an already listed PSE, and IPP is placement to Qualified Institutional Buyers only.
accepted.tq: Separate similar issue-related abbreviations by their defining feature.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment - DIPAM, strategic sale vs minority stake sale, New PSE Policy 2021

accepted.s:
With reference to disinvestment methods, consider the following statements:
1. OFS has been used widely since 2012.
2. IPP involves placement to Qualified Institutional Buyers only.
3. CPSE ETF and Bharat-22 ETF are associated with disinvestment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: OFS was widely used from 2012, IPP refers to placement only with Qualified Institutional Buyers, and CPSE ETF and Bharat-22 ETF are disinvestment instruments.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the defining feature of the method or instrument.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment - DIPAM, strategic sale vs minority stake sale, New PSE Policy 2021

accepted.s: The disinvestment policy during the period 1991–98 raised approximately:
accepted.x: Disinvestment during 1991–98 raised ₹17,557 crore, with the process being held back by coalition politics.
accepted.tq: Match the period with its specific revenue figure.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment - DIPAM, strategic sale vs minority stake sale, New PSE Policy 2021

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Establishment of the National Investment Fund
B. Renaming of the Department of Disinvestment as DIPAM
C. LIC Initial Public Offer
D. General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act amendment
accepted.x: The National Investment Fund was set up in 2005, DIPAM was renamed in 2016, the General Insurance Business Act was amended in 2021, and the LIC IPO took place in 2022.
accepted.tq: Place the dated institutional developments from earliest to latest.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment - DIPAM, strategic sale vs minority stake sale, New PSE Policy 2021

accepted.s: The shift towards strategic sales during 1999–2004 was represented by transactions involving:
o: Air India and Neelachal Ispat Nigam Ltd
accepted.x: The policy moved towards strategic sales during 1999–2004, with VSNL and BALCO cited as examples. Until 1999–2000, only minority stakes had been sold.
accepted.tq: Link the policy phase with its representative transactions.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment - DIPAM, strategic sale vs minority stake sale, New PSE Policy 2021

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the New Public Sector Enterprise Policy, 2021?
o: Maintaining a bare-minimum presence in strategic sectors
Retaining a Government enterprise in every non-strategic sector
accepted.x: The policy envisages exit from non-strategic sectors, not retention of a Government enterprise in every such sector. It retains only a bare-minimum presence in strategic sectors.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the policy direction.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment - DIPAM, strategic sale vs minority stake sale, New PSE Policy 2021

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the four strategic sector groups under the New PSE Policy, 2021?
o: Power, petroleum, coal and other minerals
accepted.x: The four groups are atomic energy, space and defence; transport and telecommunications; power, petroleum, coal and other minerals; and banking, insurance and financial services.
accepted.tq: Recall the complete classified list and identify the outside group.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment - DIPAM, strategic sale vs minority stake sale, New PSE Policy 2021

accepted.s: Which department handles closure and privatisation proposals for the non-strategic sector along with DIPAM?
o: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
accepted.x: The Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) handles closure and privatisation proposals for the non-strategic sector along with DIPAM.
accepted.tq: Use the division of responsibilities between neighbouring departments.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment - DIPAM, strategic sale vs minority stake sale, New PSE Policy 2021

accepted.s:
Which of the following trends has been associated with the recent shift from selling public enterprises to earning from them?
1. Disinvestment revenue has fallen every year except for a surge in 2022–23.
2. Dividends have grown every year.
3. A separate disinvestment heading has been removed from Budget documents.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements describe the stated trend: a general fall in disinvestment revenue with a 2022–23 surge, rising dividends, and removal of the separate disinvestment heading from Budget documents.
accepted.tq: Treat a trend question as a combined check of direction, exception and institutional presentation.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment - DIPAM, strategic sale vs minority stake sale, New PSE Policy 2021

accepted.s: The LIC Initial Public Offer of 17 May 2022 was significant because it was:
o: the first complete privatisation of a CPSE
India's biggest issue at that time
the first OFS conducted by DIPAM
accepted.x: The LIC IPO on 17 May 2022 was India's biggest issue at that time.
accepted.tq: Identify the significance attached to the dated transaction.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment - DIPAM, strategic sale vs minority stake sale, New PSE Policy 2021

accepted.x: The GIC Re OFS involved 3.39 per cent and raised approximately ₹2,345.55 crore in September 2024.

accepted.s: The General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act was amended in:

Match List-I with List-II:

B. BALCO

accepted.s: Which of the following was the first strategic sale among the listed transactions?
accepted.x: Modern Foods was the first strategic sale, undertaken in 2000, with Hindustan Lever acquiring 74 per cent.
accepted.tq: Use the year and the identifying qualifier together.
accepted.sec: Major strategic sales and privatisations → buyer

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sterlite Industries acquired 51 per cent of BALCO.
2. Hindustan Lever acquired 74 per cent of Modern Foods.
3. The buyer of Air India was Talace, a Tata Sons entity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: Sterlite acquired 51 per cent of BALCO, Hindustan Lever acquired 74 per cent of Modern Foods, and Talace acquired Air India.
accepted.tq: Verify ownership percentages and the precise buyer name separately.

accepted.s: Which statement regarding Neelachal Ispat Nigam Ltd is correct?
o: It was acquired by a Tata group steel entity, with no proceeds to the exchequer because the Centre held no equity.
It was acquired by Talace and generated proceeds for the exchequer.
Its proposed sale did not go through.
It was acquired by Sterlite Industries through a 51 per cent strategic sale.
accepted.x: Neelachal Ispat Nigam Ltd was acquired by a Tata group steel entity. The Centre received no proceeds because it held no equity in the company.
accepted.tq: Combine the buyer detail with the unusual proceeds-related qualification.

The statutory framework for Union disinvestment of CPSEs
The legal framework exclusively for municipal bonds
The legal framework for PPP projects in Andhra Pradesh, including Swiss-challenge proposals
accepted.x: The AP Infrastructure Development Enabling Act, 2001 provides the legal framework for PPP projects in Andhra Pradesh and includes Swiss-challenge proposals.
accepted.tq: Match the State statute with its specific institutional purpose.

o: Bhogapuram is a deep-water port acquired by Adani Ports in 2021.
Gangavaram is an airport developed by GMR.
Krishnapatnam Port was acquired by GMR in 2021.
Krishnapatnam Port was acquired by Adani Ports in 2020.

accepted.s: Which of the following sectors is NOT specifically covered by the draft AP PPP Policy-2026?
accepted.x: The draft policy covers transport, logistics, ports, airports, healthcare, education, renewables, tourism and urban infrastructure. Defence procurement and monetary policy are not listed.

accepted.s: The draft AP PPP Policy-2026 earmarks what amount for Viability Gap Funding (VGF)?
accepted.x: The draft AP PPP Policy-2026 earmarks ₹1,500 crore for Viability Gap Funding and proposes a bridge fund.

accepted.s: Which of the following is a major cause of stalled PPP projects?
o: Aggressive bidding, revenue shortfalls, and land or clearance delays
Automatic transfer of all risks to the Government
Guaranteed traffic growth and absence of land issues
Exclusive reliance on dividend income from CPSEs
accepted.x: Aggressive bidding, often producing the winner's curse, traffic and revenue shortfalls, and land or clearance delays can leave PPP projects stalled.
accepted.tq: Apply the risk chain from bidding assumptions to implementation failure.
accepted.sec: PPP issues - renegotiation, aggressive bidding, stalled projects, Swiss challenge method

accepted.s: The Kelkar Committee recommended that PPP contracts should have:
o: A mandatory Swiss challenge in every project
A complete prohibition on any contractual modification
accepted.x: Because unforeseen financial and implementation problems can arise, the Kelkar Committee wanted a built-in mechanism for renegotiation of PPP contracts.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional remedy proposed for a known PPP problem.
accepted.sec: PPP issues - renegotiation, aggressive bidding, stalled projects, Swiss challenge method

accepted.s: In the Swiss-challenge method, which of the following occurs first?
o: The project is referred directly to an adjudication tribunal.
The Government transfers management control to the lowest bidder without competition.
A private party submits an unsolicited proposal.
The original proponent automatically receives the contract.
accepted.x: Under the Swiss-challenge method, a private party first submits an unsolicited proposal; the Government then invites counter-bids.
accepted.tq: Test the sequence of actions rather than only the definition.
accepted.sec: PPP issues - renegotiation, aggressive bidding, stalled projects, Swiss challenge method

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Swiss-challenge method:
1. The Government invites counter-bids after receiving an unsolicited proposal.
2. The original proponent may match the best counter-bid.
3. The method is criticised for information asymmetry.
4. The Kelkar Committee encouraged its compulsory use in all PPP projects.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the Kelkar Committee discouraged the Swiss-challenge method in 2015.
accepted.tq: Spot the reversed recommendation in an otherwise accurate set of statements.
accepted.sec: PPP issues - renegotiation, aggressive bidding, stalled projects, Swiss challenge method

accepted.s: Which pair of institutions was proposed to expedite dispute resolution and project review in PPPs?
accepted.x: The Infrastructure Projects Arbitration Tribunal (IPAT) and the Infrastructure Projects Review Committee (IPRC) were proposed to speed up dispute resolution and project review.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the two proposed PPP institutions by their functions.
accepted.sec: PPP issues - renegotiation, aggressive bidding, stalled projects, Swiss challenge method

accepted.s: Which of the following is included among the current PPP-related developments?
o: Replacement of VGF by complete privatisation
Abolition of all PPP models in 2026
Revised BOT and HAM norms in May 2026
Withdrawal of the AP PPP Policy-2026
accepted.x: Current PPP developments include revised BOT and HAM norms in May 2026, NMP 2.0 for FY26–30, and the AP PPP Policy-2026 with ₹1,500 crore VGF.
accepted.tq: Select the option that fits the stated current-policy developments without reversing them.

accepted.s: Which of the following represents a criticism of asset monetisation and disinvestment?
o: Assets may be undervalued, and monetisation may be viewed as a sale by another name.
Strategic sales always increase Government ownership and control.
Dividends have disappeared completely from public enterprises.
Asset monetisation eliminates all concerns about valuation.
accepted.x: Criticisms include possible undervaluation of assets and the perception that monetisation is a sale by another name. The shift from disinvestment towards dividends is also debated.
accepted.tq: Choose the option expressing the stated criticism rather than an absolute claim.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
